title: Your week: the review
summary: The one hour a week that keeps compliance current: your agent prepares the queue, you accept or challenge each item, and the next run publishes what you accepted.

steps.title: One queue, once a week
narration: You run compliance with a few hours a week and an AI agent that does most of the reading and drafting.
hound puts everything that waits on you into one queue, each item with a recommendation.
Nothing reaches CISO Assistant without you.
Each week, CISO Assistant's task emails you the weekly review runbook. That is your cue.

panel.title: What only you can do
lines: Challenge a recommendation you are not sure of
Everything else is the agent's job: reading exports, drafting, answering your challenges

steps.title: Ask your agent to prepare the week
narration: Say to your agent: prepare this week's review.
It starts with hound next, one read-only list of everything that needs doing, most urgent first.
Here it finds manual evidence that is overdue, collectors that failed, and an exception that expires soon.
Each item names the command that fixes it, the skill the agent uses, and about how many minutes it takes.

steps.title: The agent writes a recommendation for each item
narration: Then the agent runs hound review prepare.
It refreshes the queue, lists the items that still have no recommendation, and saves the scope plan your session will apply.
For each item it records a recommendation with its reasons and its sources, so you can check what it read.
It also answers any challenge you left last week.

terminal.command: hound review recommend supplier:SUP-EXAMPLE/CTR-EXAMPLE-ASSETS --answer y --reason "ISO 27001 certificate current to 2027; holds the asset inventory only." --source inbox/example-assets-iso27001.pdf

steps.title: Your session: one command, in your own terminal
narration: Now it is your turn, in your own terminal, not the agent's.
Run hound review, and give it the time you have. For an hour, that is for sixty minutes.
It tells you how many items wait on you and takes the most urgent first.
Your turn: type the command for a one hour session.

terminal.output: 2 item(s) wait on you, about 15 minutes. This session takes 2, about 15 minutes, most urgent first.

try.prompt: Type the command that starts a one hour review session.

steps.title: Item one: a new supplier
narration: Each item shows what it is, why it matters, the recommendation, and what accepting it does.
This one is a new supplier, drafted by the agent from the vendor's documents.
The agent recommends accepting it, and names the certificate it read.
You can accept, challenge with a note, or skip. A challenge goes back to the agent, and the item comes back next week with its answer.

terminal.output:
[1/2] [supplier] SUP-EXAMPLE Example Assets Ltd: contract CTR-EXAMPLE-ASSETS (Asset inventory subscription) is a draft, covering SOL-EXAMPLE-ASSETS. Levels: dependency 2, maturity 3.
  Why it matters: A supplier is approved before any system it provides is registered, so nothing enters the scope through a supplier no one has looked at.
  Recommended: y. ISO 27001 certificate current to 2027; holds the asset inventory only. (sources: inbox/example-assets-iso27001.pdf)
  If you accept: Contract CTR-EXAMPLE-ASSETS becomes active with your name and today's date; the next scope apply writes the supplier to CISO Assistant.
a accept, c challenge, s skip, q quit:

choice.question: The recommendation gives its reason and the document it read. What do you do?

options.text: Accept: the reason is specific and the source is named.
options.feedback: A recommendation with a clear reason and a source you could open is one you can accept in a minute.

options.text: Skip it until you have read the whole contract.
options.feedback: You can, but the agent has already named what it read. Open the source if you are unsure, then decide.

steps.title: Item two: a requirement marked not applicable
narration: The next item is a requirement the agent marked not applicable, with its reasoning.
A not-applicable row leaves the audit, and an assessor will ask why, so hound always asks a person, and never covers one with a standing approval.
Read the reasoning as an assessor would.
If it does not hold up, challenge it, and say what you need.

terminal.output:
[2/2] [not applicable] EXAMPLE-ASSETS EX-2: Multi-factor authentication for privileged users.
  Reasoning: No privileged users.
  Justification: Only the supplier administers it.
  Why it matters: A not-applicable requirement is left out of EXAMPLE-ASSETS's audit; an assessor will ask why, so a person signs each one.
  Recommended: y. No privileged users. Only the supplier administers it.
  If you accept: The decision is recorded as approved by you today; it is never covered by a standing approval.
a accept, c challenge, s skip, q quit: c
Your question or objection, for the agent to answer: The supplier's admins are privileged users. Show their MFA.

choice.question: The supplier's own staff administer the system. Is "no privileged users" right?

options.text: Yes, accept it: none of our staff are administrators.
options.feedback: The supplier's administrators are still privileged users of this system. An assessor would not accept it.

options.text: Challenge it: ask for evidence of the supplier's administrator MFA.
options.feedback: Right. The item stays queued, and the agent answers your challenge before next week.

steps.title: One sign-off, one apply
narration: At the end, hound records one sign-off naming you, the time and every item.
It shows you what applying the accepted items changes in CISO Assistant, and asks once.
Commit the sign-off, and mark the week's task done in CISO Assistant.

terminal.output:
What applying the accepted items changes in CISO Assistant:
+ third party SUP-EXAMPLE Example Assets Ltd, contract CTR-EXAMPLE-ASSETS active
Apply these changes to CISO Assistant now (y, n): y
Accepted 1, challenged 1, skipped 0. Sign-off recorded in review/sign-offs/2027-02-15-091200.yaml. Your agent answers each challenge before the next session.

steps.title: Check the collectors, then you are done
narration: Last, look at hound status.
A collector that failed or has not run is the one thing to chase this week.
The standing lines say how much of each programme is met, from last month's snapshot.
Once a month, ask your agent to take the snapshot and draft the committee report. That is the routine.

terminal.output:
example-m365  2027-02-14 16:00:03  failed  0  0  -
example-m365 failed: All 2 checks errored. (collector.all_checks_errored)

choice.question: hound status shows the Microsoft 365 collector failed. What now?

options.text: Ignore it: last month's results are still in CISO Assistant.
options.feedback: Old results age out. A broken collector means those rows stop being evidenced.

options.text: Ask your agent to find out why, with hound status --json, and fix it this week.
options.feedback: Yes. The JSON names each check's problem; an expired certificate or a revoked permission is the usual cause.
